source.title: Impact of Bottleneck Layers and Skip Connections on the Generalization of Linear Denoising Autoencoders
source.authors: Jonghyun Ham; Maximilian Fleissner; Debarghya Ghoshdastidar

record.tranche_reason: The study derives and evaluates test-error behavior for two-layer linear denoising autoencoders, using a different model and analysis from the original double-descent studies.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-error curves as a function of d/n and bottleneck width, plus variance analyses relevant to the peak. Curves are mostly shown in figures without tabulated values. Epoch-wise behavior is not measured. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study derives and simulates test-error curves against c=d/n for two-layer linear denoising autoencoders, an unsupervised setting. It finds a variance-driven peak near c≈1 when n is varied at fixed d on CIFAR-10, and a second peak when d and k grow together. This bears on V3, V4 and V6 in a new model class.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with two refinements. Bottleneck width acts as an extra complexity measure with a classical bias–variance trade-off, while increasing d reduces variance; a d/n≈1 peak persists even for small k where interpolation is impossible. Skip connections attenuate the variance (an extra d^-1 factor), smoothing the peak especially when mildly overparameterized.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes two-layer linear denoising autoencoders under gradient flow, low-rank data assumptions, Gaussian input noise, and product regularization, rather than the original studies' deep-network settings. It focuses on input dimension relative to sample count and bottleneck width, not epochs.
record.method_sensitivity: Peak severity and test error depend on bottleneck width k and overparameterization; skip connections make the variance curve smoother, particularly when mildly overparameterized.
record.problems: The numerical experiments use only one trial, as the authors state. Most plotted values are not tabulated, and the theoretical analysis is restricted to two-layer linear networks with low-rank data and Gaussian noise.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported test-error or variance result was omitted. Cited findings from prior work and general background discussion are excluded.

untested.parts: Deep or nonlinear networks. The study has only two-layer linear DAEs, and model size is not swept empirically (d is fixed at 3072).
Epoch-wise test error is not measured at all.
No effective-complexity measure is defined or used to predict peak location across size, epochs and samples.
Varying label- or input-noise level; optimally tuned regularization (the analysis is ridgeless); whether the peak disappears under regularization.
Re-counting parameters with an effective-parameter measure.

missing.what: With k<r the model cannot interpolate the training data, yet the peak remains near d/n≈1. The peak location tracks d/n, not the interpolation threshold.
Theoretical statement that at fixed k and n, increasing d lowers test error through reduced variance with no bias cost. This is a model-wise second descent, in theory only.
The empirical underparameterized-side curves (d<n, from [8]) that complete the fall-rise-fall shape.
missing.locator: Figure 3 left and center, dotted lines

record.verdict_notes: V1 links were dropped: the system is a two-layer linear network, and only n was varied empirically. The study's own number for the claim (V1) does not apply to deep networks. The tranche is changed to T3 (new unsupervised denoising setting). All empirical curves are single-trial and figure only. The theory covers d≥n+r only. The reader's V6 limits_scope for skip connections was replaced with supports, since V6 does not claim skip connections remove the peak.

versions.untested_parts: The study varies input dimension relative to sample count and bottleneck width in two-layer linear DAEs; it does not test other notions of model size or nonlinear deep networks.
Test error over training epochs or training time.
The sample-size sweep is in the paper's linear DAE setting and is not a broad test across datasets or model classes.
Tests linear autoencoder variants, not a broad range of model classes.
Does not define or test whether a single effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.

The study analyzes variance and skip-connection effects on the peak, but does not vary label-noise level or regularization, test optimal regularization, or study triple or multiple descent. The relevant variance results are recorded in rows R1, R2, and R7.
Does not re-count parameters using an effective parameter measure or test whether that changes the curve to an ordinary U shape.

rows.subject: two-layer linear denoising autoencoder (without skip connections)
rows.operation_detail: Derived test-risk and variance expressions as a function of c.
rows.value: test-risk formula includes a variance term proportional to c/(c−1); text says it causes a sharp increase as c approaches 1
rows.note: The authors identify the variance term as responsible for the sharp rise near c=1.
rows.check: This is a theoretical result valid only for d≥n+r, so it covers only the overparameterized side. The variance term c/(c−1) diverges as c→1. V1 is removed.

rows.subject: two-layer linear denoising autoencoder with skip connection
rows.operation_detail: Derived test-risk and variance expressions as a function of c and compared them with the model without a skip connection.
rows.baseline: without skip connection: sharp variance rise with a (c−1)−1 factor
rows.value: with skip connection: less pronounced rise; the corresponding term has an additional d−1 factor
rows.uncertainty: asymptotic remainder terms stated in the theorem
rows.note: The study says skip connections mitigate the sharp rise, especially in the mildly overparameterized regime; they do not claim the rise is entirely removed.
rows.check: The variance term carries an extra d^-1 factor, so the peak shrinks when variance shrinks. This is consistent with V6's variance account; V6 does not claim skip connections eliminate the peak. V1 is removed.

relationships.condition: Linear DAE on CIFAR-10 (d=3072, r=100, k=50), n varied
relationships.reason: The error peaks near n≈d (c≈1), so adding samples toward d raises error (R1). With a skip connection the rise is still present but dampened (R2).
relationships.display_finding: Error rose toward a peak near n ≈ d, or c ≈ 1, and a skip connection dampened the increase.

source_check.notes: Empirical curves use one trial and provide no numerical peak heights. With k=50<r=100, the peak near n≈d is not an exact-interpolation threshold.

statements.correction: Section 5 and Figure 2: a peak persists near d/n≈1 for k<r despite impossible exact interpolation. Bottleneck width is an additional complexity measure; no unified effective-complexity predictor is evaluated. V5 verdict: none.
statements.problem: The factual description is supported, but its placement as evidence limiting V5 is unsupported: the study does not test a single effective-complexity predictor.
